_comment: Per-boss fall commentary. trigger 'boss_<biome>'. Narrator + that realm's god, both modal, played in sequence by the dialogue queue.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Hydra of Lerna lies still at last, its many heads silenced.
Where one was struck down, no two have risen to take its place. Not this time.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: The Hydra, dead — and by a mortal soul? Even Olympus did not foresee that.
Well struck, little spark. The sky will remember it.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Rangda is unmade. The demon queen's curse loosens its grip upon this realm.
Her leyak scatter back into the dark from which they crawled.

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: Balance returns by your hand, traveler. The cycle turns the cleaner for it.
But remember — Rangda is never truly gone. Nor is Barong. That is the order of things.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Apophis, the serpent of chaos, is undone. The Duat steadies on its course.
The sun's barque may sail the night-road unswallowed once more.

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: The serpent devours the sun no longer. You have the gratitude of the risen dead.
Few who enter my realm leave it having mended something. You are one.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Fenrir falls, its broken chains scattered across the frost.
Helheim itself seems to hold its breath at the sound of your name.

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: The wolf fated to swallow me whole at Ragnarök — felled early, and by you.
The runes did not foresee this. I scarce know whether to thank you or to fear you, mortal.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Orochi's eight heads lie severed in the gloom. Yomi falls quiet.
The great serpent will flood these shadows no more.

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: Orochi's shadow lifts, and my light reaches even here, into Yomi.
My brother slew this beast once, long ago. You have done it again — and for that I thank you.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Cipactli, the great devourer, is slain. Mictlan bows its bony head before you.
The earth-beast the world was built upon will swallow no more souls.

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: The devourer falls — and even I, lord of all the dead, take note of you.
You walk my nine levels as though you mean to walk out of them. Curious. Continue.
